name: mixed
description: Workable design, but estimates are never used, and deep dives only happen when pushed.
log: [00:05] Interviewer: "Hi, I'm Sam. Today let's design a URL shortener, like bit.ly, that handles 100 million new links a day. Where would you like to start?"
[00:20] Candidate: "So users give a long URL and get a short one, and visiting the short one redirects. It should be fast and scalable."
[01:00] Interviewer: "What does fast mean here, and what else matters?"
[01:10] Candidate: "Low latency on redirects, maybe under 100 milliseconds. And it should be highly available."
[02:00] Candidate: "100 million a day is around a thousand writes a second. Reads are probably more. Storage is a lot over time."
[03:00] Whiteboard: added box "Client"; added box "Server"; added box "DB"; added "Server" → "DB"
[03:30] Candidate: "The server takes the URL, hashes it with MD5, takes the first 7 characters, and stores it in the database. On a visit it looks up the code and redirects."
[04:30] Interviewer: "What happens when two URLs hash to the same 7 characters?"
[04:40] Candidate: "Hmm, then we'd have a collision. I guess we check if it exists and if so add a salt and hash again."
[06:00] Interviewer: "Which database?"
[06:05] Candidate: "Postgres, it's reliable."
[06:30] Interviewer: "At your read rate, is one Postgres enough?"
[06:40] Candidate: "Probably not, so we add a cache, like Redis, in front of it. And read replicas."
[07:00] Whiteboard: added box "Redis"; added "Server" → "Redis"
[09:00] Candidate: "We can also shard the database when it gets big."
[09:10] Interviewer: "Shard on what key?"
[09:20] Candidate: "On the short code, so lookups go to one shard."
[12:00] Interviewer: "What happens if Redis goes down?"
[12:10] Candidate: "Then requests go to the database, which might be slow, but it still works. I think that covers it."
[13:00] Interviewer: "We have time. Anything else you'd want to address?"
[13:10] Candidate: "Maybe analytics? We could log clicks to a queue. Otherwise I think that's the design."
